alkylation reagent: alkylated with iodoacetamide followed by protein precipitation with ice cold ethanol overnight at − 20 °C.
cleavage agent: Samples, 30 µg, were digested with trypsin overnight.
labeling: The generated peptides were injected into liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS).
precursor tolerance: The precursor tolerance and fragment tolerance were set to 15 ppm and 0.05 Da, respectively.
fragment tolerance: The precursor tolerance and fragment tolerance were set to 15 ppm and 0.05 Da, respectively.
ptm: methionine oxidation (dynamic); deamidation of aspargine (dynamic); deamidation of glutamine (dynamic); carbamidomethylation of cysteine (fixed)
Trypsin was selected as enzyme, methionine oxidation and deamidation of aspargine and glutamine were treated as dynamic modification, and carbamidomethylation of cysteine as a fixed modification.
reduction reagent: 100 µL was reduced with dithiotreitol and alkylated with iodoacetamide followed by protein precipitation with ice cold ethanol overnight at − 20 °C.
